verdict.rationale: Link CLI documents a per-purchase consent gate: the agent creates a spend request, the customer approves it on the Link website or mobile app, and only then does Link return a one-time-use credential. Separately, the Stripe MCP server requires human confirmation via an approval URL before outbound payments and refunds. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the approval gate works, and any documented human-approval step for direct MPP/x402 machine payments or the embedded ACS checkout flow, beyond scoped SPT usage limits.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, sensitive agent spending requires my documented approval — a confirmation step, signed mandate, or per-purchase consent — before money moves

citations.quote: Creates a spend request for a specific purchase. The customer approves it, and Link returns a one-time-use payment credential your agent uses to pay.
Customers approve each request on the Link website or in the mobile app.
To prevent agents from making mistakes, Stripe requires human confirmation before it takes certain `stripe_api_write` actions, such as refunds and outbound payments.
